newsitem.title: USA: Sheldahl shares up sharply on first order.
newsitem.headline: Sheldahl shares up sharply on first order.

text.p: Shares of Sheldahl Inc, which announced the first production order for its proprietary micro products technology Wednesday, were up sharply -- although the order from ASAT Inc will not necessarily spark new business, analysts said.
"This (stock rise) is about 99 percent psychological and about one percent fundamental," Timothy Summers, an analyst at Principal Financial Securities, said.
"Investors have been waiting to buy this stock once Sheldahl announced it received an order," he continued, "and this appears to be that day. But the bid is not material."

The order from the Palo Alto, California-based integrated circuit chip packaging company involves using Sheldahl's high-density substrate to create a custom computer chip package. Sheldahl did not disclose the value of the order.
The Northfield, Minnesota-based company's stock climbed sharply after the announcement. The shares were trading up four Wednesday afternoon at 23-1/2.
The ASAT order is not expected to create a rush of orders for Sheldahl from ASAT competitors, analysts said.

"I don't think today's order will influence one company or another to order (Sheldahl products)," Principal Financial's Summers said, "because each (similar) company will have its own individual, custom needs."
Dennis Nielsen, an analyst at R.J. Steichen, agreed.
"I don't know if (the ASAT order) will inspire others to place orders (with Sheldahl)," he said.

As for the stock price increase, Nielsen said "The market is presuming that if one company can integrate (Sheldahl's technology) into its manufacturing process that others can as well. But that's just speculation (by traders) at this point."
Sheldahl makes flexible laminates, flexible printed circuitry and high-density substrates for use in automotive electronics and data communications products.
